scope.contaminationAssessment: No OCAC lesson, title, target list, sequence, teacher material, or test item was consulted or used. Research was limited to official TBCL/CCCC capability/context references, selected CC-CEDICT item lookups, and TongXuan authority contracts. Non-contamination has not been compared or certified; no later OCAC benchmark is authorized until the TongXuan prototype is frozen.

licenseNotice.changes: Selected traditional item forms, Pinyin, and short glosses were normalized into proposal fields. Lesson targets, grammar frames, recognition timing, sequence, and rationales are TongXuan-authored hypotheses. No raw dictionary database, example sentences, test questions, audio, or images are included.

sourceCatalog.permittedUse: Selected item-level traditional/simplified forms, Mandarin Pinyin, and basic glosses, with attribution, changes stated, and share-alike maintained.
sourceCatalog.prohibitedUse: No raw-dataset ingestion in this proposal; no frequency or sequence claims; never relicense CC-CEDICT-derived data under MIT.

sourceCatalog.permittedUse: Cite broad official beginner receptive/productive capability descriptors and level context.
sourceCatalog.prohibitedUse: No copied tables or items; no reuse authorization; does not prescribe these targets, exact wording, or lesson order.

sourceCatalog.permittedUse: Cite public child-age, child-centered context and broad everyday/leisure topic scope.
sourceCatalog.prohibitedUse: No test item, question, answer, audio, image, content, or sequence reuse.

evidenceCatalog.claim: TBCL Level 1 describes simple words and phrases for personal life; Listening L-1-3 covers everyday greetings and short phrases; Speaking S-1-2 covers personal information and S-1-3 greetings/thanks. This supports broad capability scope only, not this proposal's exact expressions or sequence.

TBCL Level 2 describes simple words/phrases and short sentences for daily life; Speaking S-2-2 covers expressing self/friends' interests and interacting; Listening L-2-1 covers personal questions. This supports a possible progression endpoint, not an official five-lesson sequence or required mastery threshold.

CCCC is designed for non-native Chinese-speaking children ages 7–12, considers child cognitive/language development, and uses child-life contexts including leisure activities. This informs age/context relevance only; no CCCC task, target order, item, or expected load is copied.
CC-CEDICT item data is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Attribution, change indication, and share-alike apply. This source is not relicensed under TongXuan repository MIT.

The peer-introduction-to-preference-exchange theme, candidate targets, target load, prerequisites, recycling, and sequence are TongXuan hypotheses. TBCL/CCCC do not mandate them. Frequency evidence is unavailable in the cited lexical source and remains UNVERIFIED.

Character-level SRS is UNRESOLVED. Character recognition is proposed separately; no character ID is placed in srsReviewTargets because the cited framework and lexical references do not support a character-level review/mastery unit.

lessons.whyNow: Start with a personal-life message and everyday greeting. TBCL Level 1 supports that capability; choosing self-name as the first outcome is a TongXuan hypothesis.
lessons.orderRationale: No earlier curriculum target is required; oral greeting and self-identification establish the communicative base.
alternatives: Begin with greetings only and defer names.
Use a non-verbal name card outside this language target set.

lessons.title: L2 — Ask and answer a peer's name
lessons.whyNow: Once the learner can identify themself, add the matching question addressed to a peer. This makes Lesson 2 depend on Lesson 1 rather than introducing a parallel topic.
lessons.orderRationale: Requires Lesson 1 self-identification and its question/answer ingredients; the learner now directs a personal question to a peer.
alternatives: Teach only a fixed name-response frame and defer the question word.
Ask for one-word responses before productive question forms.

lessons.title: L3 — Tell a peer one preference
lessons.whyNow: Use the known peer/name exchange as the interaction context for one personally relevant preference and one concrete leisure noun. The exact lexical choice and order are hypotheses.

alternatives: Use a learner-selected noun only after its provenance and load are reviewed.
Omit the fixed leisure noun until child validation.

lessons.title: L4 — Ask what a peer likes
lessons.whyNow: Transfer the already-known what-question from names to preferences. No new vocabulary is added; the new target is the question pattern and its reciprocal listening/response move.
lessons.orderRationale: Requires the Lesson 3 preference statement and Lesson 2 question word; the learner transfers a familiar question function to personal interests.
alternatives: Keep only the statement pattern and postpone asking about interests.
A yes/no question would require a separate negative-response policy.

lessons.title: L5 — Sustain a reciprocal introduction-and-preference exchange
lessons.whyNow: Add 呢 as a short turn-return prompt, then integrate greeting, name exchange, preference question, answer, and turn return. This is a new discourse capability, not a REVIEW-only activity.
lessons.orderRationale: Requires the Lesson 1–4 lexical and interaction chain; the learner returns the preference prompt and maintains reciprocal turns.
alternatives: Integrate Lessons 1–4 without 呢; that would make Lesson 5 consolidation rather than a new discourse capability.
Use another sourced reciprocal-turn device after evidence review.
